notes.subject: plate
notes.text: White plates with a blue field on the left holding gold letters RKS, a two-digit district code, the state emblem, a three-digit number from 101, a dash and two letters.

notes.subject: plate
notes.text: The two-digit code marks the district: 01 to 07 cover the capital area and six other districts.

notes.subject: plate
notes.text: The two serial letters only run from A up to Q.

notes.subject: plate
notes.text: Plates from the UN administration era (1999 to 2010) carry the letters KS between three-digit numbers; some are still used for cross-border trips.

notes.subject: plate
notes.text: Police vehicles have red characters; export plates have a blue background with white characters.

notes.subject: plate
notes.text: Security force vehicles have dark green plates with yellow characters and the letters FSK.

notes.subject: plate
notes.text: International force vehicles carry blue plates with white characters and the prefix KFOR; UN mission plates show UNMIK across the top.

notes.subject: plate
notes.text: Old-timer plates contain the word HISTORIK and a seated goddess symbol.

notes.subject: plate
notes.text: Cars with plates issued by the northern neighbour, showing its own district codes, are still seen in the Serb-majority north after a 2022 plate-switch dispute.

notes.subject: language
notes.text: Two official languages, with the country name written in both Latin and Cyrillic script.

notes.subject: landscape
notes.text: Varied terrain of high plains, rolling hills and mountains, some above 2,500 m, with a mainly continental climate.

notes.subject: other
notes.text: The phone code is +383, and the .xk web domain has only been proposed.
